title: Information Theory: From Questions to Communication
summary: Entropy and coding, dependency and noisy channels, and information divergence as a bridge between probability, communication, and statistics. Proof ideas, explicit binary calculations and hypotheses accompany the mathematical statements.
assumed_background: Probability of discrete events, elementary logarithms, and willingness to work with sums.

lectures.title: From Information to Compression: Entropy, Questions, and Codes
lectures.description: Motivates entropy through optimal questions, derives prefix-tree constraints and relates expected code length to Shannon limits.

lectures.title: Information Through Noise: Dependence, Data Processing, and Channel Capacity
lectures.description: Calculates dependency from a noisy messenger, proves data processing via chain rules, and explains binary-channel capacity and reliable coding.

lectures.title: Why a Wrong Probability Costs Logarithmic Evidence
lectures.description: Derives KL as excess expected log loss and ties it to likelihood estimation, calibration and limits of fitting.
